To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a sieve element specific ENDO like protein is a novel phytocyanin that is expressed only in the phloem and that has a role in the reproductive development of Arabidopsis.

an ENOD like protein accumulates in the plasma membrane of the sieve element, but not the companion cell, and is a member of a multigene subfamily of ENOD like proteins that are encoded by a gene family that includes both gametophytic and phloem specific ENOD like proteins.
a monoclonal antibody, RS6, recognizes a protein, ENOD, that is expressed specifically in the sieve element plasma membranes of Arabidopsis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the sieve element specific RS6 antigen as an ENOD like protein and its potential role as an essential membrane protein in sieve elements of Arabidopsis.
the identification and characterization of the RS6 sieve element specific antigen and the role of this phytocyanin in sieve element function and development.

the molecular characterization of an early nodulin like protein that is expressed in the sieve element plasma membranes of the phloems of both vegetative and reproductive tissues in the model plant Arabidopsis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a novel phytocyanin is a plasma membrane anchored protein that accumulates in the sieve element plasma membranes of Arabidopsis and is a member of a family of ENOD like proteins that are expressed in the phloem of both floral and vegetatively growing Arabidopsis.

the sieve element specific RS6 antigen is a novel member of the ENOD family of phytocyanin proteins and is a potential candidate to play a role in the physiological functioning within the sieve element.
the RS6 antibody recognizes a 21.5-kD sieve element plasma membrane protein that is encoded within a gene family of ENOD like proteins that are members of the cupredoin superfamily.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sieve element specific RS6 antigen is an ENOD-like protein encoded by the gene At3G20570.
a sieve element plasma membrane associated protein that is encoded from a gene expressed in gametophytically derived tissues has an essential role during reproductive development.

the sieve element specific At3g205700 gene is a member of the ENOD like subfamily of cupredoxin proteins that is specifically expressed in sieve elements and has an essential role in the functioning of the pholem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Arabidopsis phloem sieve elements express a novel ENOD like protein that is attached to their plasma membrane via a glycosylphoshatidyl inositol membrane anchor.
sieve elements in Arabidopsis contain an ENOD like protein and that this protein is expressed in a sieve element companion cell specific manner.

sieve element specific ENO D like proteins are expressed at the earliest stages in the differentiation of sieve elements and that the ENOD like protein identified by the RS6 monoclonal antibody is likely to be an important component of the sieve element plasma membranes.
